provinces.name: Mittelmark
provinces.layer_b_text: The Mittelmark is the empire's granary — flat, endlessly fertile plains drained by the Avar's tributaries. Grain elevators stand taller than the churches. The population is dense but rural; towns are market hubs for surrounding farmland rather than centers of culture. The Governor's seat is Kornstadt, a prosperous and deeply boring administrative city. Political life in the Mittelmark is dominated by the great grain-owning families who have held their land for generations and resent Vareth's tax demands with practiced precision. The biggest threat here is not monsters but drought, blight, and the slow encroachment of land consolidation that forces small farmers off their plots.

settlements.name: Kornstadt
settlements.note: Provincial capital. Grain exchanges, imperial administration, three competing noble families. Wide streets, massive grain silos visible from twenty km.

settlements.name: Mühlenbach
settlements.note: Mill town on tributary river. Flour trade. Known for a recurring bandit problem on the northern road.

settlements.name: Auerfeld
settlements.note: Eastern Mittelmark market town. Trade crossroads. Essenz crystal trade from Bergrand province passes through.

settlements.name: Sumpfrand
settlements.note: Western edge of province, near Waldreiche border. Quiet, insular, does not trust Vareth.

static_npcs.name: Lena Marsh
static_npcs.description: A competent agricultural administrator in her mid-forties from a grain-owning family. Manages the province effectively and creatively interprets tax law in her family's favor.
static_npcs.personality: Practical, land-loyal, dismissive of Vareth politics. Polite surface, hard interest beneath.
static_npcs.schedule_summary: Kornstadt palace weekdays, travel to major estates on rotation

provinces.name: Nordmark
provinces.layer_b_text: The Nordmark is the empire's northern border and its roughest edge. The Gebirgsstaaten loom on the horizon — their fortress-cities visible on clear days from the Nordmark's hillforts. The border is not formally closed but is heavily watched. Smugglers bring Essenz crystals from the Gebirgsstaaten mines at better prices than the Große Waagehalle offers, which creates a permanent low-level tension between imperial customs enforcement and the local economy that depends on the trade. The population is hard, practical, and militarized — three generations of proximity to the Gebirgsstaaten has produced people who maintain their walls and train their children with weapons. The garrison here is the best-equipped in the empire outside Vareth itself.

settlements.name: Grenzwall
settlements.note: Fortress-city on the border ridge. Half civilian, half military. The Grenzwall garrison is 3000 soldiers. Significant Essenz smuggling operation disguised as legitimate crystal trade.

settlements.name: Bergpasstor
settlements.note: Controls the main mountain pass into Gebirgsstaaten territory. Everything moving through gets checked twice.

settlements.name: Feldlager Ost
settlements.note: Military outpost, essentially. Few civilians. Junction of two border roads.

settlements.name: Händlerstadt
settlements.note: The border trade town. Gebirgsstaaten merchants come here officially. Unofficially, much more happens.

static_npcs.name: Rolf Stenn
static_npcs.description: A large man in his fifties with a veteran's deliberate movements and a career built on keeping the border quiet at all costs. Does not care about politics. Cares intensely about logistics and loyalty.
static_npcs.personality: Blunt, fair within the military context, deeply pragmatic. Will ignore minor smuggling if it keeps the peace. Will not ignore anything that threatens the border's integrity.

provinces.name: Flusstal
provinces.layer_b_text: The Flusstal is the empire's wine country — the upper reaches of the Avar river, where the valley narrows and the slopes catch enough sun to grow the dark grapes that produce Flusstal red, the most exported wine in the empire. The nobility here is old, minor, and proud — families who have held the same hillside vineyards for two hundred years and regard Vareth as an upstart. The towns are small and civilized. The roads are good. The politics are intricate, involving ancient disputes over water rights, vintage precedence, and inheritance claims that have been in the imperial courts for decades. Monsters are rare — the valley is long-settled and patrolled — but the deeper forest on the valley rim still harbors things that take livestock.

settlements.name: Weinmark
settlements.note: Provincial capital and wine market. The autumn wine fair is the largest gathering in the province. Noble houses maintain townhouses here.

settlements.name: Oberstrom
settlements.note: Upper Avar river junction. River trade hub, less refined than Weinmark, more practical.

settlements.name: Rebburg
settlements.note: Hillside wine village, famous for a single estate's vintage. Deeply insular.

provinces.name: Ostmarsch
provinces.layer_b_text: The Ostmarsch is the empire's eastern edge — sparse, flat, and poorly mapped. The land grades gradually into the Steppenvölker territory without a clear natural boundary, which makes it perpetually contested. Imperial presence thins rapidly east of the main road: a chain of watchtowers, semi-permanent patrol camps, and the occasional fortified village that is really just a garrison with civilians attached. The Steppenvölker raid here in the dry years — not conquest, but opportunistic: livestock, stored grain, the occasional valuable prisoner. The local population is either very tough or recently moved in to replace those who were not.

settlements.name: Ostfort
settlements.note: Easternmost significant settlement. Military compound with civilian market. Supply depot for the watchtower chain.

settlements.name: Wachturm-Kette (7 towers)
settlements.note: Seven watchtowers spaced 15km apart along the frontier road. Each holds 20 soldiers and signal equipment.

provinces.name: Seeprovinz
provinces.layer_b_text: A scattered province of Binnenmeer islands — fourteen inhabited, fifty more seasonal or uninhabited. The Seeprovinz has the empire's most powerful naval force and its most autonomous character. Island populations have always been harder to tax and govern than mainland ones. The Provincial Governor rules from Inselkron on the largest island and has, over three governors, developed what amounts to a private fleet. The islands produce fish, salt, and strategic position — they control the shipping lanes between the western Binnenmeer and the eastern ports. Everyone with a ship has an opinion about the Seeprovinz.

settlements.name: Inselkron
settlements.note: Capital island. Naval headquarters, governor's compound, major trading port. The Imperial Navy's Third Fleet is based here.

settlements.name: Salzinsel
settlements.note: Salt production island. The salt mines here supply a quarter of the empire's salt. Hard labor, essential product.

settlements.name: Grüne Insel
settlements.note: Officially a fishing village. Unofficially a resupply point for vessels that prefer not to use licensed ports. The governor knows. His fleet needs to know where the ships are.

static_npcs.name: Cessa Vol
static_npcs.description: The most powerful naval commander in the empire, a fact she is careful never to make too obvious in Vareth. Early fifties, sun-damaged skin, the compact economy of movement of someone who has lived on ships.
static_npcs.personality: Strategic, patient, loyal to the navy before the emperor. Keeps her options open without committing to anything she cannot walk back.

provinces.name: Bergrand
provinces.layer_b_text: The Bergrand sits at the imperial foothills — where the flat plains begin to buckle upward toward the Gebirgsstaaten mountains. Mining is the dominant industry: iron, copper, and occasional Essenz-bearing crystal deposits that are modest compared to the Gebirgsstaaten mother lodes but still economically significant. The mining towns are company towns — owned or controlled by the great mining houses, who have their own security forces and their own relationship with the Governor that is less administration and more negotiation. Workers in the Bergrand mines live hard and spend their wages in company-controlled taverns. The ore they extract is what keeps the empire's weapons sharp.

settlements.name: Erztal
settlements.note: Mining capital. Company headquarters, smelting district, workers' quarter. The Great Erztal Mine is three km north of the city.

settlements.name: Kristallgrube
settlements.note: Essenz crystal mining town. Most valuable mine in the province. Heavy imperial customs presence.

settlements.name: Hammerstadt
settlements.note: Secondary mining and forging town. The hammers run day and night. Noise is a constant.

provinces.name: Tiefebene
provinces.layer_b_text: The deep interior of the Ostimperium — flat, agricultural, and far from everything interesting. The Tiefebene is not a place people go to; it is a place they are from. Three large rivers cross it on their way to the Avar, creating a rich but quiet agricultural heartland that produces grain, livestock, and very few notable events. The population is large, rural, and suspicious of strangers — not out of hostility but out of the insularity that comes from generations of self-sufficiency. The main economic tension is between the independent farming families and the increasingly large estate-holders who buy out smaller farms. In the last twenty years, three large family farms per year have been absorbed into noble estates. The dispossessed farmers go to Vareth or join the roads.

settlements.name: Breitfeld
settlements.note: Administrative center of the province. Grain storage capital. The Breitfeld Grain Exchange sets prices for the surrounding 200km.

settlements.name: Dreifluss
settlements.note: Where three rivers meet. Boat building, river trade, a permanent floating market on the confluence.

settlements.name: Südliche Dorfkette
settlements.note: Cluster of seven villages along a southern road. Each about 5km apart. Agricultural, quiet, increasingly nervous about estate consolidation.
